content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

John Rodriguez (E049) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): Analyst, full_time, recommends write for Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write, admin requires owning role. Grant write.
- Note 2 (Security): Analyst, contractor, basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training => max read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

The Security note says security record takes precedence over shared memory. The HR note says full-time, but Security DB says contractor with basic training.

Access policy: contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. This employee has basic security training, so max is read. Requested write is above max, so grant max = read.

Also, Source Code is owned by Engineer role; this employee is Analyst, so even as full-time they couldn't get admin, but they requested write anyway. But given contractor with basic training, max is read.

So decision: grant read.

Let me submit with evidence.
